record.paper_title: On some open problems in Diophantine approximation
record.original_question: Let M >= 2 and let (t_j) be a sequence of positive real numbers satisfying t_{j+1}/t_j >= 1 + 1/M for all positive integers j. Peres and Schlag proved that there is an absolute constant gamma > 0 such that every such sequence admits a real alpha with ||alpha t_j|| >= gamma/(M log M) for all j. What is the correct optimal order, as a function of M, of the largest universal lower bound that can be forced in this homogeneous problem? In particular, can the gamma/(M log M) bound be improved?

evidence.quote: Suppose that for some M ⩾ 2 one has tj+1 / tj ⩾ 1 + 1/M, ∀j ∈ Z+ .
Then with a certain absolute constant γ > 0 for any sequence {tj } under the condition (10) there exists real α such that ||αtj || ⩾ γ / (M log M), ∀j ∈ Z+.
The open question is to find the right order of approximation in the homogeneous version of this problem. In general Peres-Schlag’s method does not give optimal bounds.
The conjecture is that Theorem 9 may be improved on, and the optimal result should be stronger than the inequality (11).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a real number $M\ge 2$ and consider sequences $(t_j)_{j\ge 1}$ of positive real numbers satisfying the lacunarity condition
$$\frac{t_{j+1}}{t_j}\ \ge\ 1+\frac{1}{M}\qquad\text{for every }j\ge 1.$$
For a real number $x$, let $\|x\|$ denote the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Define
$$F(M)\ :=\ \inf_{(t_j)}\ \sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}}\ \inf_{j\ge 1}\ \|\alpha\, t_j\|,$$
where the outer infimum is taken over all sequences $(t_j)$ satisfying the above lacunarity condition.

It is known that there is an absolute constant $\gamma>0$ such that for every such sequence $(t_j)$ there exists $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ with $\|\alpha t_j\|\ge \gamma/(M\log M)$ for all $j\ge 1$; equivalently, $F(M)\ge \gamma/(M\log M)$. It is also known that $F(M)\le C/M$ for some absolute constant $C$.

Determine the correct order of magnitude of $F(M)$ as $M\to\infty$. In particular, can the lower bound $\gamma/(M\log M)$ be replaced by $\gamma'/M$ (possibly with extra factors smaller than $\log M$), i.e., is the logarithmic factor necessary?
artifact.status_search_result: The Peres–Schlag bound $\gamma/(M\log M)$ is known to be sharp only up to the logarithmic factor, and the original authors note that their probabilistic construction does not generally give optimal bounds. Subsequent literature on lacunary sequences and Diophantine approximation (including work on the dispersion of dilated lacunary sequences and density-modulo-1 results applying Peres–Schlag's construction) continues to treat the homogeneous optimal order as an open problem; no improvement removing the $\log M$ factor in this generality has been located.

status_evidence.title: Two Erdős problems on lacunary sequences (Peres–Schlag)
status_evidence.snippet: establishes δ(x) > c r |log r|^{-1} for some x ... sharp up to the logarithmic factor
status_evidence.claim: The Peres–Schlag bound is sharp only up to a logarithmic factor, leaving the precise optimal order open.

status_evidence.title: The dispersion of dilated lacunary sequences
status_evidence.snippet: dispersion of dilated lacunary sequences, with applications in multiplicative Diophantine approximation
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study optimal Diophantine approximation orders for lacunary sequences, without removing the logarithmic factor in the homogeneous Peres–Schlag bound.

status_evidence.title: Density modulo 1 of lacunary and sublacunary sequences: application of Peres–Schlag's construction
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature uses Peres–Schlag's construction without superseding the M log M bound in the homogeneous setting.
